reference: Physical values from NASA/JPL public data. Semi-major axis in AU. Temperatures in Celsius. Radiation tier 1 (low) to 5 (extreme).

bodies.name: Moon
bodies.objective: Pass within 100 km and return 20 images
bodies.description: Earth's natural satellite. No atmosphere, extreme temperature swings, and constant micrometeoroid bombardment. The proving ground for every deep space mission.

bodies.name: Mars
bodies.objective: Enter orbit and map the surface for 30 sols
bodies.description: The red planet. Thin CO2 atmosphere, global dust storms, and the best evidence for past water in the solar system. Launch windows open every 26 months.

bodies.name: Venus
bodies.description: Earth's twin gone wrong. Surface pressure is 92 times Earth's and hot enough to melt lead. Any lander is a short-lived triumph.

bodies.name: Mercury
bodies.objective: Enter orbit and map the surface
bodies.description: The closest planet to the Sun. No atmosphere, extreme thermal swings, and solar radiation flux eleven times stronger than Earth's orbit.

bodies.name: Ceres
bodies.description: The largest object in the asteroid belt. Microgravity, subsurface ice, and the first stepping stone to the outer system.

bodies.name: Europa
bodies.objective: Pass within 500 km and scan the ice shell
bodies.description: An icy moon with a subsurface ocean. The most promising place to look for life beyond Earth, inside one of the harshest radiation environments in the solar system.

bodies.name: Titan
bodies.description: Saturn's largest moon. The only moon with a dense atmosphere, with methane lakes and rivers on the surface. Sunlight is 1% of Earth's.

bodies.name: Uranus
bodies.objective: Pass within 10,000 km and return atmospheric data
bodies.description: The tilted ice giant. Only visited once, by Voyager 2 in 1986. Light delay is over two hours one way, so the spacecraft must fly itself.

bodies.name: Triton
bodies.objective: Pass within 1,000 km and return surface imagery
bodies.description: Neptune's largest moon. Orbits backwards, suggesting it was captured. Nitrogen geysers erupt from its surface. The coldest place ever measured in the solar system.

bodies.name: Pluto
bodies.objective: Pass within 2,000 km and return all science data
bodies.description: The most distant world ever visited. Sunlight is 0.06% of Earth's. The New Horizons flyby in 2015 was a nine-year journey for a few hours of data.
